name: Tithing In The New Testament
overview: The New Testament understanding of tithing is rooted in the Old Testament practice where God established the giving of a tenth as an act of worship and provision for the Levites, who served in the tabernacle (Numbers 18:21, 26). The giving of tithes was a tangible expression of faith and dependence on God's provision, as seen in Jacob's vow to God for sustenance and protection (Genesis 28:20). The Lord commanded that tithes be brought into the storehouse to support His work and promised abundant blessings for faithful giving (Malachi 3:10). These foundational principles highlight tithing as a covenantal act of trust and stewardship that continues to inform the believer’s response to God’s grace.
